rationale: The book's identification of righteousness as the doing of God's commandments (the law kept and worn as righteous acts) is the best-supported reading of the supplied definitional texts and garment symbolism. Deut 6:25, Ps 119:172 and 1 John 3:7 explicitly equate righteousness with observing/doing the commandments; Rev 19:8 (dikaiōmata) makes the wedding garment consist of those performed acts, which the chapter shows are given yet must be worn, washed and kept. This unifies the OT multi-witness pattern, the garment/armor imagery (Isa 61:10; Eph 6; Zech 3; etc.), and the prior accepted cores (belief, faith and love all require obedient submission/command-keeping) more tightly than the common primary reading. The strongest counter (forensic status imputed by faith as the definition, with doing as mere fruit) must reclassify the plain definitional statements and plural 'acts' as secondary or metaphorical; the chapter's reframing of the same garment texts as covenant-worn obedience answers that counter without contradiction. Residual Pauline tension is real but does not overturn the direct lexical evidence or produce a superior overall explanation of the supplied material.
book_core_identification: Righteousness is the doing of God's commandments—the law kept
book_secondary_elaborations: worn as the garment of righteous acts (Rev 19:8 dikaiōmata)
covenant covering given then enacted/washed/kept (linked to kanaph, baptism, foot-washing, armor of God)
strongest_counter_interpretation: Righteousness primarily denotes forensic/imputed right standing before God (Christ's righteousness credited to the believer by faith alone), with ethical commandment-keeping as subsequent fruit rather than the definition itself; garment imagery symbolizes that covering status.
counter_core_identification: forensic right-standing / imputed status received by faith
material_core_denial: The counter denies that righteousness is defined as the performance of the commandments, treating commandment-keeping either as non-justifying 'works of the law' or as the fruit of an already-received verdict.
counter_case: Rom 4:3-8 / Gen 15:6: righteousness counted/credited by faith apart from works
Rom 1:17; 3:21-26; Phil 3:9: righteousness of God revealed/given through faith in Christ, not own law-righteousness
2 Cor 5:21: believers become the righteousness of God in him
Isa 61:10 robe and traditional Protestant reading of garment texts as pure covering/status
book_explanatory_advantages: Direct definitional match to the three printed verses (Deut 6:25 'it shall be our righteousness if we observe to do'; Ps 119:172 'all thy commandments are righteousness'; 1 Jn 3:7 'he that doeth righteousness is righteous')
Accounts for the plural active dikaiōmata of Rev 19:8 as the actual substance of the wedding garment without collapsing deeds into status
Integrates 'given' (Rev 19:8; Eph 2:10) with required wearing/washing/keeping, avoiding both fig-leaf self-righteousness and purely passive verdict
Consistent with the book's OT multi-witness method and with prior FULL findings that faith, belief and love all entail obedient response to the word
counter_explanatory_advantages: Strongly organizes the dense Pauline cluster on justification by faith and 'righteousness of God' as gift
Explains exclusion of works of the law from the basis of justification (Rom/Gal)
Fits traditional Protestant forensic reading of the Abraham narrative and garment covering
unresolved_objections: Precise integration of 'apart from works of the law' with 'the law kept' as righteousness itself (which commandments; role of faith as already defined in prior findings)
Whether every use of 'righteousness of God' is fully exhausted by the enacted-acts reading
